subject: Q4 runway allocation & batching/cache scenarios — QBR input
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 28 Oct 2027 16:10:00 -0700
Subject: Q4 runway allocation & batching/cache scenarios — QBR input

Team —

Putting together the infra section for the QBR deck and need a short, defendable appendix on capacity runway and unit economics that leadership can consume quickly. Key asks:

- Short (1-paragraph) summary of our runway risk assuming a 2.5x burst in hosted request volume for 6 weeks starting mid-Nov.
- Two scenario tables: (A) conservative (no extra reserved GPUs, rely on bursting + fallback routing) and (B) aggressive (reserve additional capacity for Dedicated customers + prefer low-latency clusters).
- Updated unit-econ delta for each scenario (per-token GPU cost, end-to-end tail latency impact, and expected cost savings from prefix caching + continuous batching).

I've attached the current modeling workbook and a short PDF of the batching/cache simulation outputs. Please review the assumptions (tab: assumptions) and the demand curve I used (tab: demand_curve).

Deliverable: 1) a 2-slide summary (bullet + small table) we can drop into the QBR main deck, and 2) an appendix slide with the full model link. Can you each add a 1-2 line note about operational risk and a suggested ask (e.g., reserve X GPUs, enable aggressive prefix caching) by Monday EOD?

Attachments: runway_alloc_modeling_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet), batch_cache_simulations.pdf (pdf)

Thanks —
Mina
Mina Haddad
Director, Platform Economics
Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 29 Oct 2027 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Q4 runway allocation & batching/cache scenarios — QBR input

Thanks Mina — quick read-through and a few flags inline.

On Thu, Oct 28, 2027 at 4:10 PM Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com> wrote:
> Team —
> 
> Putting together the infra section for the QBR deck and need a short, defendable appendix on capacity runway and unit economics that leadership can consume quickly. Key asks:
> 
> - Short (1-paragraph) summary of our runway risk assuming a 2.5x burst in hosted request volume for 6 weeks starting mid-Nov.
> - Two scenario tables: (A) conservative (no extra reserved GPUs, rely on bursting + fallback routing) and (B) aggressive (reserve additional capacity for Dedicated customers + prefer low-latency clusters).
> - Updated unit-econ delta for each scenario (per-token GPU cost, end-to-end tail latency impact, and expected cost savings from prefix caching + continuous batching).
> 
> I've attached the current modeling workbook and a short PDF of the batching/cache simulation outputs. Please review the assumptions (tab: assumptions) and the demand curve I used (tab: demand_curve).

Notes:
- The 2.5x baseline looks plausible for the hosted trial we have with Acme (they indicated a November spike) but we should present a middle scenario (1.6x) to avoid scaring the execs.
- For the conservative table, call out the expected P95 tail increase (estimate +18–25% latency) when we rely solely on spot/burst capacity.
- We should show a small incremental savings line for caching that reflects realistic hit rates (20–35% prefix hit depending on customer). Don't use the optimistic 60% hit rate in the current assumptions tab.

Operational ask: if we commit to reserved capacity in Scenario B, we should specify the minimum committed window (90 days) and impact on gross margin; finance will need that number.

I'll draft the 2-slide summary and drop the deck link into the Drive folder by Monday.

Laura Bennett
VP, Product — Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, laura_bennett@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 30 Oct 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Q4 runway allocation & batching/cache scenarios — QBR input

Adding a couple of concrete numbers and attaching a trimmed workbook with updated cost assumptions.

Highlights (see attachment: runway_alloc_modeling_v2.xlsx, sheet: summary):
- Baseline (no spike): avg GPU utilization 62%, per-token infra cost $0.00095.
- 2.5x spike (6 weeks) without reservations: expected avg util drops to 41% across pooled clusters (due to skewed concurrency), per-token infra cost rises to ~$0.00145 when factoring in preemption and cross-region fallbacks.
- Scenario B (reserve 40 rGPU-equivalent units across two regions): keeps tail latency P95 within +6% of baseline and reduces per-token cost to ~$0.00105 (includes amortized reservation premium).
- Caching + continuous batching: modeled 25% prefix hit rate and batching improvements reduce per-token compute by ~18% in both scenarios; end-to-end latency improves more for common short requests (<=128 tokens).

Attachment: runway_alloc_modeling_v2.xlsx (updated assumptions, scenario outputs)

Operational risk note: reservations buy latency stability but reduce flexibility. If finance cannot commit to 90-day minimums, we should prepare a hybrid fallback policy that pins critical enterprise routes to reserved clusters and allows hosted public routes to remain opportunistic.

Vivek
Head of Infrastructure Economics
Redwood Inference
From: Taylor Reed <taylor.reed@acme-ops.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: Acme Finance <finance@acme-ops.com>
Date: Mon, 01 Nov 2027 08:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Q4 runway allocation & batching/cache scenarios — QBR input

Thanks for the heads up, Mina and team — appreciate the modeling detail. A few clarifications from Acme side:

- The spike is driven by a product launch scheduled for week of Nov 15. We expect sustained traffic for ~5 weeks, but peak concurrency is likely concentrated in the first 10 days.
- We are open to a short-term committed capacity arrangement if it guarantees sub-300ms P95 for our production routes.
- Can you confirm whether prefix caching will be isolated per-customer? We want a cache eviction policy that prevents cross-customer pollution.

If you can confirm the caching isolation and give a recommended committed capacity (rGPU eq.), Acme can make a finance-side decision quickly.

Taylor Reed
Head of Platform — Acme Corp
Attachments: none
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, laura_bennett@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, Taylor Reed <taylor.reed@acme-ops.com>
Date: Fri, 05 Nov 2027 14:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Q4 runway allocation & batching/cache scenarios — QBR input

Good thread — concise next steps so we can close this before the QBR: 

1) Mina/Vivek: finalize Scenario A/B numbers using Vivek's updated sheet; include a middle (1.6x) column to appease execs. Drop the two-slide summary in the Drive folder and add a one-line recommended ask (reserve vs hybrid). Deadline: Monday, Nov 8 COB.
2) Mina: confirm caching isolation policy and outline eviction strategy (per-customer namespaces + TTL tiers).
3) Laura: prepare the financial impact line for reserved capacity (90-day commit cost vs expected gross margin delta).
4) Taylor/Acme: if you can, confirm desired rGPU eq. for the first 10-day peak window; we will model that exact profile.

I'll take the QBR appendix slide and make sure the leadership deck includes the runway risk callout.

-Markus
VP, Infrastructure Strategy
Redwood Inference
